head_commit.message:
chore(deps): sentry 0.49 with tauri-plugin-sentry 0.6, gated at the wire (#984)

* chore(deps): drop the no-op reqwest rustls-native-certs feature

reqwest 0.13.1 exposed `rustls-native-certs` only as the implicit feature
of an optional dependency it never references in its own source, so
enabling it changed nothing: OS trust roots already arrive through
`rustls-platform-verifier` (pulled by reqwest's `rustls` feature) and
through the system stack behind `native-tls`.

reqwest 0.13.2 removed the optional dependency, which turns the stale
entry into a hard resolve error. Unblocks any bump that floats reqwest
past 0.13.1.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(deps): bump sentry 0.42 -> 0.49 with tauri-plugin-sentry 0.6

The coordinated bump dependabot could not do. tauri-plugin-sentry 0.6
builds against sentry 0.49, so the plugin-only PR (#972) duplicated
sentry/sentry-core/sentry-types in the lock; both sides move together
here. sentry-rust-minidump follows transitively, 0.13 -> 0.17 (its
lib.rs is byte-identical between the two, so no supervisor API change).

Re-verified the four traps the Cargo.toml comment block records:

* Single copy — sentry, sentry-core, sentry-types all resolve to exactly
  one 0.49.1, shared by the app, the plugin, and the minidump crate. The
  stale reqwest 0.12 lock entry sentry 0.42 dragged along is gone, so
  reqwest is now single-version too (0.13.4).
* Transport — `ureq` and `native-tls` still exist as features in 0.49
  and still select `UreqHttpTransport`; sentry's resolved deps are
  httpdate, native-tls, sentry-*, ureq, with no reqwest and no tokio.
  0.49 also adds `logs` + `metrics` to its defaults; both stay off, they
  are new egress surfaces ADR-0020 never consented to.
* Capability — `sentry:default` still expands to allow-envelope +
  allow-breadcrumb in the generated ACL manifest, unchanged from 0.5.
* Init + consent — init still runs before tauri::Builder and still forks
  the supervisor from the same call. `ClientOptions` became
  #[non_exhaustive] in 0.49, so the struct literal moves to the builder;
  every field keeps its previous value.

No paired npm package exists: the browser SDK is a js_init_script inside
the crate, so there is nothing on the JS side to bump.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(deps): reconcile the lock after rebasing over the dependabot bumps

* fix(crash-reporting): enforce consent and drop opaque envelopes at the wire

Security review found real, new egress in tauri-plugin-sentry 0.6, and a
claim of mine that was simply false. `before_send` is not the last hop:
it has exactly one call site in sentry-core 0.49.1 (client/mod.rs:383,
inside the capture_event preparation). Anything handed to
`Client::send_envelope` reaches the transport with no callback between.

The plugin uses that door. When a renderer envelope fails to parse — it
routinely does, because @sentry/vite-plugin's debug-ID injection writes
a `debug_meta` sourcemap image sentry-rust cannot deserialize — 0.6
rebuilds it via `Envelope::from_bytes_raw` and calls `send_envelope`
(commands.rs:30-35). Those bytes live in a private `Items::Raw` that
`to_writer` copies to the socket verbatim, so no redaction of ours can
reach inside. Plugin 0.5 dropped them; 0.6 ships them.

So the guarantee moves to the only place that sees every byte. A
`GuardedTransportFactory` wraps the SDK's own DefaultTransportFactory
(ureq under our features) and enforces, per envelope:

  * consent, re-read from an atomic mirror of the consent file. This
    also closes the mid-session opt-out hole: `Hub::current()` is
    thread-local, so `disable_current` only unbound the calling thread,
    and the plugin's own Client clone in Tauri state never consults a
    hub at all.
  * opaque envelopes dropped, restoring 0.5's semantics. A payload we
    cannot inspect is one we cannot redact; the privacy guarantee
    outranks the sourcemap edge case. Counted and logged content-free.

flush/shutdown delegate, so the supervisor's pre-exit flush still works.

Also here:
  * `.enable_logs(false)` / `.enable_metrics(false)`. Both default to
    TRUE in 0.49 (0.42 had them off) and the field is not cfg-gated, so
    any future crate enabling `sentry/logs` would unify the feature in
    and open the pipe silently.
  * deny.toml bans `failspot/enabled` — a fault-injection crate riding
    in under the crash reporter, inert as locked (its lock entry has no
    dependencies, so `dep:flagset` is off) and it must stay that way.
  * Corrected three comments this falsified: lib.rs on renderer events
    inheriting before_send, the module docs on where redaction is
    enforced, and `disable_current`'s claim to drop "every subsequent
    event".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(crash-reporting): stop overclaiming what the options test guards

Mutation-checking my own test found one assertion that does not guard
what its doc said it did. Deleting `.send_default_pii(false)` leaves the
test green, because `false` is also `ClientOptions::default()` — so that
line catches a wrong value but not a deleted call, and no test could
distinguish the two.

The other six were each verified by deletion: transport, before_send,
before_breadcrumb, enable_logs, enable_metrics, server_name all turn the
test red when their builder call is removed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(crash-reporting): scope the cold-path claim and pin the bump checklist

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat(pipeline): phase 4 — the max generation depth (#970)

* feat(pipeline): max-depth section artifact types

The typed answers one max-depth section call may return, plus the seeds a
section is generated FROM. The split between SectionSeed and the *Out
types is the core rule expressed as types: identity, project links and
education lines are seeded from the source and the model authors only the
presentation. JudgeItem deliberately has no severity field, so the
Warning-only cap is structural rather than a filter.

* feat(pipeline): per-section generation for max depth

One structured call per resume section, in a fixed source-gated order, with
every answer filtered before it is kept: unbacked citations dropped, a
skill the source never states removed, an education entry that is not a
verbatim copy discarded, and a project's name/links/stack re-seeded from
the source whatever the model returned. The fan-out checks the run
deadline between calls and treats one section's failure as one section,
never as the run's.

The projects-format primitives (entry boundaries, link detection, the
description-line cap) are re-exported from validate::content rather than
re-implemented, so the generator and the checks that grade its output
cannot disagree about a truthful document.

* feat(pipeline): assemble the max-depth sections into a resume body

The finished sections become the SAME plain-text body the quality draft
produces, so validate, repair, the report, the editor and the exporters
see one shape at both depths. The layout is code-owned: the identity line
is rendered in the form split_entry reads back, consecutive employment
entries share one heading, and the projects ladder renders exactly the
three shapes consistency.project_structure accepts — a project the source
never described gets the compact link line, never a filler blurb.

The progressive stream appends the same bytes the document will carry, so
what the user watches build is what the run assembles.

* feat(pipeline): run the staged pipeline at max depth

max_pipeline() + MAX_STAGES, Budget::RESUME_MAX and its own run deadline,
and the L3 wiring that lets one execute() serve both depths through three
lookups instead of two copies of the shell. RunHooks gains the
section-wise half: per-section pipeline:stage events with sectionKey
filled (validated by the generated grammar) and the progressive document
stream on the existing ai:stream channel, display-only at both depths.

The max deadline deliberately does NOT buy the re-ask worst case the
quality one does: 3h20m is a backstop no user sits through, and a max run
stopped mid-fan-out keeps the sections it already assembled.

* feat(pipeline): the max-depth llm judge, warning-only and skippable

One structured call reviewing the finished document, contributing advisory
judge.* Warnings to the report. Three structural caps: JudgeItem has no
severity field, every issue is built with Severity::Warning written at the
construction site, and every failure mode (provider error, expired
deadline, refused daily cap, unparseable answer) records a reason code and
returns Ok — the judge can never fail a run.

Deviation from the settled stage order, with the reason: the judge runs
AFTER repair, not between validate and repair. repair replaces ctx.report
with the one it re-validated, so notes merged in earlier are dropped on
exactly the documents that were repaired, and a quote taken before a
repair names text the finished document no longer contains.

* feat(pipeline): regenerate one max-depth entry from its persisted artifacts

At max depth the strategy and evidence artifacts are persisted in FULL
alongside their counts, in the DB event row only — ADR-027 is the LOG
boundary and the log lines stay counts-only. A later 'regenerate this
role' click reads them back and rebuilds exactly that entry through the
same generate_one and the same assemble the run used, splicing only its
line range so the other roles cannot change.

Every miss is soft: a quality run, a non-experience key, a run older than
the detail, an artifact the store's clamp truncated, or an entry the
document no longer has all fall back to the whole-section rewrite. A click
must not fail because an optimization was unavailable.

* style(pipeline): satisfy clippy on the max-depth tests

assertions_on_constants: two shipped budgets compared at runtime prove
nothing a const block does not prove at build time. filter_next: rfind.

* feat(renderer): enable max generation depth

The staged pipeline runs max now, so the depth flag flips and the panel
sends the depth the user picked instead of the quality literal. The
unavailable note follows the same rule as the run: both staged depths
need the same server-resolved inputs, so it shows for either.

* feat(renderer): map the max-depth stages onto the run machine

`sections` and `assemble` are max depth's split of `draft`; `llm_judge`
runs last, after repair, and reads the finished document, so it maps to
the checking state rather than the repairing one. A max run therefore
ends its stage trail in `validating` — still busy, because no stage
event may ever end a run.

* feat(renderer): fold per-section progress off the stage stream

Max depth reports each section through the same `pipeline:stage`
channel, so the session hook folds `sectionKey` + phase into a
per-section map. Only states an event proves are written: `queued` is
not observable (the wire carries the STAGE's index/total and the section
counts ride in the persisted artifact), and neither validate nor repair
attributes its counts to a section, so verdicts stay with the report.

* feat(renderer): live section timeline for a max-depth run

A checklist of the sections the run has actually reported, in generation
order, hosted next to the stage dots. No placeholder rows: the roster
depends on the strategy's company plan and never reaches the renderer,
so a pre-drawn list would name sections that may never be generated. An
experience entry is numbered rather than given a company name the
content-free wire never carried.

* docs(renderer): the display-only stream carries max depth's assembly too

Nothing was gating the stream on depth, so nothing needed ungating: both
depths ride one `ai:stream` under the run's umbrella job. The doc said
"the draft stage's deltas", which is only half of what arrives now, and
a test pins that the pane renders the progressively assembled text
without a branch — still display-only.

* feat(renderer): label the max-depth judge's remarks as model-written

A `judge.*` message is the model's own prose about this document, not a
label for a fixed check, so the panel renders it verbatim: the namespace
short-circuits the catalog lookup structurally, before `i18n.exists`,
rather than relying on nobody adding the key. It carries a provenance
badge — the note is free text derived from an untrusted posting, and it
stays an inert text node. Per-section repair attribution still does not
exist at either depth; the note in SectionVerdicts now says so.

* feat(shared): a max-depth run deadline the client can be held above

Mirrors `timeouts::max_run_deadline` (6900 s fixed + one effort-scaled
pass, 7200–7800 s) so the renderer has a bound that stays ABOVE the
backend's at every tier — the side that knows why a run stopped has to
give up first. Hand-mirrored rather than generated, because gen:ipc does
not emit the Rust constant; the per-tier table is pinned as literals on
both sides so the pair cannot drift silently.

* fix(pipeline): f2 — join a per-entry regenerate on identity, never on position

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(renderer): give the section ladder the `done` rung it needs

`PipelineSectionState` never had `done`, so the fold that writes it on a
`sections` finish did not type-check — vitest runs esbuild and said
nothing; `tsc` caught it. Folding onto `checking` instead would claim a
check that has not started, so the type gains the rung the plan's ladder
always described. `max` is also a runnable stored depth now, so the
preference coercion needs a value from outside the vocabulary to stay
reachable.

* fix(pipeline): f3 — let the zero-call stages run when the deadline expires

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): f4 — delete a posting's run trail with its application

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): f5, f6 — re-cap the report after the judge and count its call

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): f7, f8 — keep the artifact detail off the wire, order partial section lists in place

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): f9-f12 — charge the judge's call, keep the entry separator, drop dead helpers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(shared): re-sync the max-run deadline with the recomputed backend

The Rust fix round counts the judge as the 24th flat-bounded call, so
`MAX_RUN_FIXED_SECS` is 7_200 and the per-tier table moves to
7_500…8_100 with a 125-minute budget floor. The fan-out assertion is now
strict: the pre-judge 6_900 put the bottom tier exactly level with the
calls it wraps, and a deadline that leaves the last call no room to
return is the binding constraint this derivation exists to avoid.

* fix(pipeline): f10 — a repair round that loses content is worse than the count says

round_is_worse keeps its count term and gains an absence term: a round is
worse if the candidate carries an absence-shaped Critical (code, evidence)
pair the draft did not. Absence-shaped is factual.dropped_role plus
factual.altered_project_link's absence arm, discriminated by the same
evidence-presence test report::fabrications uses to keep that arm out of the
review panel — so the two places that decide what an absence is cannot
disagree.

Pairs, not codes: a document that already lost a role stays repairable, while
a round that swaps WHICH employer is missing is caught.

This also closes the pre-existing QUALITY-depth hole. It is the same loop and
the same draft: a rewrite that traded two fabricated metrics for one dropped
employer scored 1 < 2, was kept, and deleted a job from the saved resume —
with no reviewable finding for the user to act on, because an absence has no
span.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(renderer): make the section timeline audible and honestly live

The host's stage caption cannot announce section progress: a section
event carries the STAGE's index/total, so its text is frozen for the
whole sections stage and an unchanged live region says nothing — one
utterance, then silence for the run's longest phase. Adds the prep
panel's milestone announcer (sr-only, once per transition) and a
written-count the sighted user can watch move, counted against sections
SEEN because the roster is not on the wire. The list is a list again:
role="group" dropped list semantics for a rationale that role never
controlled. Depth-agnostic unavailable copy now that max is selectable,
the always-visible max summary carries the two-hour cue, and an
unparseable entry index renders "?" instead of NaN.

* fix(pipeline): h1 — reorder employment entries as one block under one heading

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): h2 — join a per-entry regenerate on the whole seeded triple

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): h3 — cascade the run trail when a generated resume is deleted

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): m1, m2 — hand apply_stop the stage, and floor what a stopped run may overwrite

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): m3 — one spelling of a posting url in the runs store

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): round-2 lows — evidence pin, marker edge, and the accepted trades

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): normalize an imported run's job url, and gate the persist floor on the outcome

A restore bound run.job_url raw while every other write site normalized, so
any backup taken before the normalization landed restored rows no reader and
no delete could reach: the runs panel came back empty, delete_for_job matched
nothing and still reported success, both cascades silently no-opped, and the
strategy/evidence detail outlived the owner meant to remove it. data_import
runs against the live store with no re-open, so the open-time sweep never got
a chance either.

is_persistable now needs the run to have FAILED, not merely to carry a stop
reason: stages::repair records RunTimeout/Budgeted for a recovered in-loop
stop and returns Ok, and repair is quality depth's last stage — so a
completed run over a source with no employment section silently saved nothing
while reporting completed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): gate the save on the source's work history, not on the run

is_persistable read the run instead of the documents, and both readings were
wrong in their own direction. The stop reason refused a completed run over a
source with no employment section once repair hit the daily cap; the outcome
missed the case the gate exists for, because the sections fan-out treats a
cap refusal as Budgeted, breaks, and returns Ok - and nothing downstream
turns that into an Err. A max run capped right after Summary therefore had
outcome Ok and overwrote the saved resume with a summary-only document.

Comparing the two documents answers both: refuse only when the source has an
employment section and the draft does not. A new-grad or academic CV can
never trip it; a truncated fan-out over a real work history always does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): purge the run trail only after the parent delete commits

Five advisory findings from the ensemble round.

The applications cascade fired before s.delete and was not gated on it, so a
SQLITE_BUSY or IO failure left the application alive with its trail already
irreversibly gone - the ordering ai_generations_remove refuses by name. The
max deadline's two terms are now emitted by gen-ipc-rust.ts beside the
quality pair instead of living as two independent literals whose TS-side doc
claimed they could not drift. The judge's dropped counter no longer charges
cap-truncated valid remarks as verbatim-quote failures. plan_sections'
budget trim now reports what it cut, so a 13-slot plan losing Education is
visible in the artifact instead of silent.

Three stale comments corrected: max depth is admitted now, report_section
hardcodes attempt 1 like its sibling, and a per-section cache key buys
collision avoidance rather than per-entry invalidation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(contract): the staged pipeline runs both depths now

* docs: update phase 4 (max depth) from planned to shipped state

* fix(pipeline): bound bulk-delete parameter lists and spare a kept generation's trail

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): report a refused save as a failed run, never a keyless section event

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): drop unrenderable sections, hide missing evidence, parse once

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(pipeline): lead the max deadline doc with its summary, share one note cap

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(knowledge): point the max pipeline docs at their source symbols

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): a run whose posting was deleted mid-flight abandons its own output

upsert_run is INSERT OR REPLACE and save_application is a merge-upsert, so a
run that finished after its posting was deleted re-inserted the run row and
re-created the ai_generations aggregate - the posting came back in the runs
panel, the Documents list and the next backup, with a permanently partial
trail because the pre-purge events were already gone. Confirmed by running
it: purge, one event appended into the gap, terminal upsert, row back with 1
event where the run produced 2.

The run now checks its own row at the terminal write. Gone means some delete
door removed this posting - applications, ai_generations, factory reset or a
restore - so the run skips persist, skips the row, sweeps the gap's events
and reports cancelled. A terminal check rather than cancel-and-await because
nothing maps a job_url to an in-flight run's cancel token, and the in-flight
window would land here regardless.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat(pipeline): phase 4 — the max generation depth (#970)

* feat(pipeline): max-depth section artifact types

The typed answers one max-depth section call may return, plus the seeds a
section is generated FROM. The split between SectionSeed and the *Out
types is the core rule expressed as types: identity, project links and
education lines are seeded from the source and the model authors only the
presentation. JudgeItem deliberately has no severity field, so the
Warning-only cap is structural rather than a filter.

* feat(pipeline): per-section generation for max depth

One structured call per resume section, in a fixed source-gated order, with
every answer filtered before it is kept: unbacked citations dropped, a
skill the source never states removed, an education entry that is not a
verbatim copy discarded, and a project's name/links/stack re-seeded from
the source whatever the model returned. The fan-out checks the run
deadline between calls and treats one section's failure as one section,
never as the run's.

The projects-format primitives (entry boundaries, link detection, the
description-line cap) are re-exported from validate::content rather than
re-implemented, so the generator and the checks that grade its output
cannot disagree about a truthful document.

* feat(pipeline): assemble the max-depth sections into a resume body

The finished sections become the SAME plain-text body the quality draft
produces, so validate, repair, the report, the editor and the exporters
see one shape at both depths. The layout is code-owned: the identity line
is rendered in the form split_entry reads back, consecutive employment
entries share one heading, and the projects ladder renders exactly the
three shapes consistency.project_structure accepts — a project the source
never described gets the compact link line, never a filler blurb.

The progressive stream appends the same bytes the document will carry, so
what the user watches build is what the run assembles.

* feat(pipeline): run the staged pipeline at max depth

max_pipeline() + MAX_STAGES, Budget::RESUME_MAX and its own run deadline,
and the L3 wiring that lets one execute() serve both depths through three
lookups instead of two copies of the shell. RunHooks gains the
section-wise half: per-section pipeline:stage events with sectionKey
filled (validated by the generated grammar) and the progressive document
stream on the existing ai:stream channel, display-only at both depths.

The max deadline deliberately does NOT buy the re-ask worst case the
quality one does: 3h20m is a backstop no user sits through, and a max run
stopped mid-fan-out keeps the sections it already assembled.

* feat(pipeline): the max-depth llm judge, warning-only and skippable

One structured call reviewing the finished document, contributing advisory
judge.* Warnings to the report. Three structural caps: JudgeItem has no
severity field, every issue is built with Severity::Warning written at the
construction site, and every failure mode (provider error, expired
deadline, refused daily cap, unparseable answer) records a reason code and
returns Ok — the judge can never fail a run.

Deviation from the settled stage order, with the reason: the judge runs
AFTER repair, not between validate and repair. repair replaces ctx.report
with the one it re-validated, so notes merged in earlier are dropped on
exactly the documents that were repaired, and a quote taken before a
repair names text the finished document no longer contains.

* feat(pipeline): regenerate one max-depth entry from its persisted artifacts

At max depth the strategy and evidence artifacts are persisted in FULL
alongside their counts, in the DB event row only — ADR-027 is the LOG
boundary and the log lines stay counts-only. A later 'regenerate this
role' click reads them back and rebuilds exactly that entry through the
same generate_one and the same assemble the run used, splicing only its
line range so the other roles cannot change.

Every miss is soft: a quality run, a non-experience key, a run older than
the detail, an artifact the store's clamp truncated, or an entry the
document no longer has all fall back to the whole-section rewrite. A click
must not fail because an optimization was unavailable.

* style(pipeline): satisfy clippy on the max-depth tests

assertions_on_constants: two shipped budgets compared at runtime prove
nothing a const block does not prove at build time. filter_next: rfind.

* feat(renderer): enable max generation depth

The staged pipeline runs max now, so the depth flag flips and the panel
sends the depth the user picked instead of the quality literal. The
unavailable note follows the same rule as the run: both staged depths
need the same server-resolved inputs, so it shows for either.

* feat(renderer): map the max-depth stages onto the run machine

`sections` and `assemble` are max depth's split of `draft`; `llm_judge`
runs last, after repair, and reads the finished document, so it maps to
the checking state rather than the repairing one. A max run therefore
ends its stage trail in `validating` — still busy, because no stage
event may ever end a run.

* feat(renderer): fold per-section progress off the stage stream

Max depth reports each section through the same `pipeline:stage`
channel, so the session hook folds `sectionKey` + phase into a
per-section map. Only states an event proves are written: `queued` is
not observable (the wire carries the STAGE's index/total and the section
counts ride in the persisted artifact), and neither validate nor repair
attributes its counts to a section, so verdicts stay with the report.

* feat(renderer): live section timeline for a max-depth run

A checklist of the sections the run has actually reported, in generation
order, hosted next to the stage dots. No placeholder rows: the roster
depends on the strategy's company plan and never reaches the renderer,
so a pre-drawn list would name sections that may never be generated. An
experience entry is numbered rather than given a company name the
content-free wire never carried.

* docs(renderer): the display-only stream carries max depth's assembly too

Nothing was gating the stream on depth, so nothing needed ungating: both
depths ride one `ai:stream` under the run's umbrella job. The doc said
"the draft stage's deltas", which is only half of what arrives now, and
a test pins that the pane renders the progressively assembled text
without a branch — still display-only.

* feat(renderer): label the max-depth judge's remarks as model-written

A `judge.*` message is the model's own prose about this document, not a
label for a fixed check, so the panel renders it verbatim: the namespace
short-circuits the catalog lookup structurally, before `i18n.exists`,
rather than relying on nobody adding the key. It carries a provenance
badge — the note is free text derived from an untrusted posting, and it
stays an inert text node. Per-section repair attribution still does not
exist at either depth; the note in SectionVerdicts now says so.

* feat(shared): a max-depth run deadline the client can be held above

Mirrors `timeouts::max_run_deadline` (6900 s fixed + one effort-scaled
pass, 7200–7800 s) so the renderer has a bound that stays ABOVE the
backend's at every tier — the side that knows why a run stopped has to
give up first. Hand-mirrored rather than generated, because gen:ipc does
not emit the Rust constant; the per-tier table is pinned as literals on
both sides so the pair cannot drift silently.

* fix(pipeline): f2 — join a per-entry regenerate on identity, never on position

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(renderer): give the section ladder the `done` rung it needs

`PipelineSectionState` never had `done`, so the fold that writes it on a
`sections` finish did not type-check — vitest runs esbuild and said
nothing; `tsc` caught it. Folding onto `checking` instead would claim a
check that has not started, so the type gains the rung the plan's ladder
always described. `max` is also a runnable stored depth now, so the
preference coercion needs a value from outside the vocabulary to stay
reachable.

* fix(pipeline): f3 — let the zero-call stages run when the deadline expires

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): f4 — delete a posting's run trail with its application

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): f5, f6 — re-cap the report after the judge and count its call

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): f7, f8 — keep the artifact detail off the wire, order partial section lists in place

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): f9-f12 — charge the judge's call, keep the entry separator, drop dead helpers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(shared): re-sync the max-run deadline with the recomputed backend

The Rust fix round counts the judge as the 24th flat-bounded call, so
`MAX_RUN_FIXED_SECS` is 7_200 and the per-tier table moves to
7_500…8_100 with a 125-minute budget floor. The fan-out assertion is now
strict: the pre-judge 6_900 put the bottom tier exactly level with the
calls it wraps, and a deadline that leaves the last call no room to
return is the binding constraint this derivation exists to avoid.

* fix(pipeline): f10 — a repair round that loses content is worse than the count says

round_is_worse keeps its count term and gains an absence term: a round is
worse if the candidate carries an absence-shaped Critical (code, evidence)
pair the draft did not. Absence-shaped is factual.dropped_role plus
factual.altered_project_link's absence arm, discriminated by the same
evidence-presence test report::fabrications uses to keep that arm out of the
review panel — so the two places that decide what an absence is cannot
disagree.

Pairs, not codes: a document that already lost a role stays repairable, while
a round that swaps WHICH employer is missing is caught.

This also closes the pre-existing QUALITY-depth hole. It is the same loop and
the same draft: a rewrite that traded two fabricated metrics for one dropped
employer scored 1 < 2, was kept, and deleted a job from the saved resume —
with no reviewable finding for the user to act on, because an absence has no
span.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(renderer): make the section timeline audible and honestly live

The host's stage caption cannot announce section progress: a section
event carries the STAGE's index/total, so its text is frozen for the
whole sections stage and an unchanged live region says nothing — one
utterance, then silence for the run's longest phase. Adds the prep
panel's milestone announcer (sr-only, once per transition) and a
written-count the sighted user can watch move, counted against sections
SEEN because the roster is not on the wire. The list is a list again:
role="group" dropped list semantics for a rationale that role never
controlled. Depth-agnostic unavailable copy now that max is selectable,
the always-visible max summary carries the two-hour cue, and an
unparseable entry index renders "?" instead of NaN.

* fix(pipeline): h1 — reorder employment entries as one block under one heading

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): h2 — join a per-entry regenerate on the whole seeded triple

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): h3 — cascade the run trail when a generated resume is deleted

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): m1, m2 — hand apply_stop the stage, and floor what a stopped run may overwrite

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): m3 — one spelling of a posting url in the runs store

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): round-2 lows — evidence pin, marker edge, and the accepted trades

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): normalize an imported run's job url, and gate the persist floor on the outcome

A restore bound run.job_url raw while every other write site normalized, so
any backup taken before the normalization landed restored rows no reader and
no delete could reach: the runs panel came back empty, delete_for_job matched
nothing and still reported success, both cascades silently no-opped, and the
strategy/evidence detail outlived the owner meant to remove it. data_import
runs against the live store with no re-open, so the open-time sweep never got
a chance either.

is_persistable now needs the run to have FAILED, not merely to carry a stop
reason: stages::repair records RunTimeout/Budgeted for a recovered in-loop
stop and returns Ok, and repair is quality depth's last stage — so a
completed run over a source with no employment section silently saved nothing
while reporting completed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): gate the save on the source's work history, not on the run

is_persistable read the run instead of the documents, and both readings were
wrong in their own direction. The stop reason refused a completed run over a
source with no employment section once repair hit the daily cap; the outcome
missed the case the gate exists for, because the sections fan-out treats a
cap refusal as Budgeted, breaks, and returns Ok - and nothing downstream
turns that into an Err. A max run capped right after Summary therefore had
outcome Ok and overwrote the saved resume with a summary-only document.

Comparing the two documents answers both: refuse only when the source has an
employment section and the draft does not. A new-grad or academic CV can
never trip it; a truncated fan-out over a real work history always does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): purge the run trail only after the parent delete commits

Five advisory findings from the ensemble round.

The applications cascade fired before s.delete and was not gated on it, so a
SQLITE_BUSY or IO failure left the application alive with its trail already
irreversibly gone - the ordering ai_generations_remove refuses by name. The
max deadline's two terms are now emitted by gen-ipc-rust.ts beside the
quality pair instead of living as two independent literals whose TS-side doc
claimed they could not drift. The judge's dropped counter no longer charges
cap-truncated valid remarks as verbatim-quote failures. plan_sections'
budget trim now reports what it cut, so a 13-slot plan losing Education is
visible in the artifact instead of silent.

Three stale comments corrected: max depth is admitted now, report_section
hardcodes attempt 1 like its sibling, and a per-section cache key buys
collision avoidance rather than per-entry invalidation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(contract): the staged pipeline runs both depths now

* docs: update phase 4 (max depth) from planned to shipped state

* fix(pipeline): bound bulk-delete parameter lists and spare a kept generation's trail

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): report a refused save as a failed run, never a keyless section event

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): drop unrenderable sections, hide missing evidence, parse once

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(pipeline): lead the max deadline doc with its summary, share one note cap

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(knowledge): point the max pipeline docs at their source symbols

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): a run whose posting was deleted mid-flight abandons its own output

upsert_run is INSERT OR REPLACE and save_application is a merge-upsert, so a
run that finished after its posting was deleted re-inserted the run row and
re-created the ai_generations aggregate - the posting came back in the runs
panel, the Documents list and the next backup, with a permanently partial
trail because the pre-purge events were already gone. Confirmed by running
it: purge, one event appended into the gap, terminal upsert, row back with 1
event where the run produced 2.

The run now checks its own row at the terminal write. Gone means some delete
door removed this posting - applications, ai_generations, factory reset or a
restore - so the run skips persist, skips the row, sweeps the gap's events
and reports cancelled. A terminal check rather than cancel-and-await because
nothing maps a job_url to an in-flight run's cancel token, and the in-flight
window would land here regardless.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: integrate the no-ai-slop catalog into the anti-ai-tell system (#967)

* feat: integrate the no-ai-slop catalog into the anti-ai-tell system

Curates all ~90 catalog items through a four-rule checkability bar (fixed
form, zero factual content, unconditional prompt ban, no hidden domain
meaning): eight high-precision entries join the validated lexical tier
(paramount, transformative, multifaceted, ever-evolving, paradigm shift,
meticulous, widely regarded as, it is worth noting), ~44 items — including
every construction pattern (binary contrasts, colon reveals, fake-profound
kickers, portability test, show-don't-tell) — become prompt guidance the
model is instructed by but user text is never flagged for, and ~19 are
skipped with recorded reasons. Zero structural checks shipped: both
candidates fired on truthful counter-examples ("shipped a status page,
showcasing live latency"; a polite self-answered close) — the family
already removed twice. Words naming real work (utilize, facilitate,
spearhead, beacon) stay validator-invisible by rule, pinned by negative
controls over an ordinary resume; apostrophe-bearing entries are blocked by
a shape test (matching never normalizes punctuation, so they were half-dead
by construction); German stays curated-not-translated with a leak pin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: depth-aware guidance tier and the critic advisories on the tell catalog

The anti-tell blocks split into checked and guidance tiers per depth: brief
ships exactly the lines that back a voice.* check (the validator cannot see
which depth produced the output, so brief may only instruct what it also
verifies), dropping the block share of the small-model letter prompt from
48 to 26 percent; full and task keep the complete text and every other call
site is byte-identical via the depth default. The voice formatting line is
scoped so it no longer contradicts the letter's keyword-bolding output
rules, pinned by a prompt-consistency test. transformative moves to the
prompt tier — it fails the catalog's own no-hidden-domain-meaning rule on
transformative learning and transformative justice, both now negative
controls. Curly apostrophes fold to ascii at the two ai_tell_issues call
sites only (header-name matching untouched), making contraction tells
checkable: it's worth noting, it's important to note and the today's-world
filler join their frequent surface forms — the uncontracted twins needed
their own entries, the for-free hypothesis tested false. Shape guards gain
double-space and leading-non-word checks; the German construction-guidance
asymmetry is recorded as an evidence-driven deferral.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: ensemble findings — depth everywhere, honest tiers, paramount out

The depth tiering reaches all nine prose consumers instead of two:
referral, application-email, rewrite and the interview and answer builders
thread their resolved depth (the last three gained a backward-compatible
target param), roughly halving every small-model system prompt — a brief
referral note drops from 7129 to 4140 chars. The CHECKED constants now
carry only validator-backed phrases: ten prose phrases and nine lexical
strays the module's own tests classify as never-validated moved to the
guidance tier, enforced by a mechanical reverse test that parses the
quoted bans out of the checked lines (a bogus phrase added there now
fails it), shrinking the brief blocks further. paramount moves to the
prompt tier — Paramount Global is a real employer and the exemption reads
only the resume, never the job ad; the employer-name exemption widening is
recorded as a deferral with its injection risk noted (company name, not ad
body). The intermediate-commit baselines are reworded to what main
actually shipped, the budget bound ratchets to a quarter, the opener
matcher folds curly apostrophes like its siblings (with a contraction
opener appended and the load-bearing indices documented), and the vacuous
bold-ban iteration is replaced by unguarded cases per ban-bearing depth.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: coderabbit round-1 findings on the voice-block composition and test rigor

The application-email builder composed its voice block only in the full
branch — brief and task carried no anti-tell rules at all, the format
skeleton's two opener examples being the entire anti-slop surface; the
depth-scoped block is now hoisted into one local composed by all three
branches (full byte-identical), pinned per depth with mutations failing
exactly the branch they remove. The opener tests assert through a
first_evidence Option so a miss names the fixture; the letter negative
control gains the genuinely missing template-opener silence pin while four
comments naming a voice.ai_tell_prose code that never existed are
corrected; the honesty test's normalize folds curly apostrophes like the
matcher it mirrors; and the quoted-ban parser throws loudly on an
unbalanced quote instead of silently shifting every later ban into prose.

head_commit.message:
feat: autopilot adopts semantic scoring when enabled (#966)

* feat: autopilot adopts semantic scoring when enabled

Scheduled runs re-rank the keyword prefilter's top survivors through the
same combined kernel as the jobs page — score_one semantics including
languages_align, closing the known divergence on this path — when the user
has semantic scoring on. The webview-only toggle gets a rust-readable
single-column mirror on job_preferences written by settings and boot-sync,
deliberately not a struct field so the full-row set() can never clobber it
(the salary_expectation precedent). Phase two runs after cluster_aware_retain
so minMatchScore keeps its keyword meaning and only deduped survivors cost
an embed, capped at twenty per run from the aggregator's posting cap;
cache ids hash canonical_job_key and the resume text so tracking-param
variants hit the paid row and a resume edit is a miss by construction.
Embed failure degrades that job to keyword-only via an explicit scoreSource
emitted from the same option check as the blend — a run never fails because
of scoring, and the formula version stays unbumped because no score changes.
The autopilot percent label flips to match percent only when semantic is on,
en and de.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: critic blockers on the autopilot semantic re-rank

The translate flag becomes a MatchSurface enum with one shared translates()
table — every surface labelled match percent runs the full jobs-page
pre-processing including translation (the skipped step collapsed coverage
to language-neutral tokens and embedded a cross-lingual cosine, two
different numbers under one label), false only for the extension's
structural zero-egress; pinned by a cross-surface parity test. The
synthetic resume snapshot vector moves out of the shared vectors index into
posting_vectors with its TTL discipline, the write site itself now refuses
synthetic scoring ids (documents/sql.rs split for R8), and a test pins the
index count and stale arithmetic across a semantic run. The tautological
semantic-off test is replaced by should_semantic_rerank plus a phase
function owning the gate, the wall clock (per-run timeout with keyword-only
degrade and a rerank_start step) and a lazy setup closure, so zero-cost-off
is a property of the tested function. Re-ranked head and keyword tail sort
as two blocks; only cluster canonicals are re-ranked (an unreachable
belt-and-braces dedup guard was deleted rather than shipped); daily-cap
charges move inside score() behind an actual-round-trip predicate; the
autopilot locale source now matches the jobs page with detect-and-backfill
recorded as a deferral; mirror-write failures surface a notification.
